correctness.rationale: Reconstructs the entire n>=2 claim. The binary exponents are nonnegative; dyadic binomial expansion mod4 is established by induction. All summands have identical degree. The marked-part generating function determines multiplicity sums modulo2; B(n) even n>=2 justifies exact division by two. Odd-index pairing is bijective. Q(1)=1 proves the exact finite-field root multiplicity, and d>=2^t ensures polynomiality. Independently computed all coefficients for n=2..100, plus the coefficient of x and kernel root. No extrapolation from finite testing.

originality.rationale: Full original paper arXiv:2605.10512v1 Sections 1 and 4 (24 pages) and follow-up arXiv:2605.21718v1 Sections 1 and 4 (15 pages) inspected in material parts. The first establishes exact recurrence, binary partition pair identity, low coefficient congruences; second establishes coprimality. Neither states closed all-degree mod4 dyadic trace kernel and exact large root multiplicity. published-finding corpus queries for aliases, congruences, roots and half numerator returned no equivalent covering statement. Two own-ledger periods checked. Residual risk from exact recurrence and unindexed derived formulas explicitly acknowledged.
residual_risks: An equivalent closed coefficientwise modular congruence may exist in unindexed literature.

Ballantine et al. already give a full characteristic-zero recurrence from which the new congruence could be derived by nontrivial simplification; novelty claimed only for explicit closed trace kernel and root multiplicity, not for generic computability.

value.rationale: This is an explicit all-degree, all-index prime-adic structural theorem for natural partition rational numerators, not an isolated coefficient or normalization test. It turns arbitrarily large polynomial congruence profiles into a degree-2^t kernel indexed only by a binary valuation and one bit, and gives exact unbounded multiplicities of the characteristic-two root -1. The problem is motivated by the source’s open coefficient-shape and polynomial arithmetic questions, without claiming to settle shape conjectures.
